name: Sacroiliitis
definition: Inflammation of one or both sacroiliac joints caused by axial spondyloarthritis, infection or other inflammatory disorders; mechanical SI pain is a separate diagnosis.

redFlags.item: Severe acute unilateral pain with bacteremia risk

investigations.principle: Cause-directed laboratory and imaging assessment is required.
investigations.MRI: MRI SI joints is sensitive for active inflammatory sacroiliitis in the appropriate context.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs identify structural sacroiliitis but may be normal early.

amber: Suspected infection requires urgent antimicrobial/infectious disease management.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Shroni/Kati Shotha phenotype may be documented only after inflammatory/infectious classification.

patientEducation.summary: Inflammation of one or both sacroiliac joints caused by axial spondyloarthritis, infection or other inflammatory disorders; mechanical SI pain is a separate diagnosis.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise, rapidly escalating pain or other listed red flags.
